sourceEvidence.excerpt: INT/INTEGER: Used for whole numbers.
SMALLINT: Used for smaller whole numbers.
SMALLINT can store values like 32767 or -32768.
TINYINT can hold integer values ranging from 0 to 255
BIGINT: Used for large whole numbers.
DECIMAL(p, s)/NUMERIC(p, s): Used for fixed-point numbers
FLOAT: Used for single-precision floating-point numbers.
REAL: Another term for single-precision floating-point numbers.
REAL can store values similar to FLOAT.
DOUBLE: Used for double-precision floating-point numbers.
CHARACTER or CHAR(n): Fixed-length character string
the default is set to one.
CHARACTER VARYING or VARCHAR(n): Variable-length character string
TEXT: Designed to store large blocks of variable-length text data.
TEXT can store long paragraphs or documents.
htmlDescription mediumtext
BINARY(n): Fixed-length binary data.
BINARY VARYING or VARBINARY(n): Variable-length binary data.
BINARY LARGE OBJECT or BLOB
BLOB can store large binary files like an image file.
image mediumblob
DATE: Used for date values (year, month, day).
DATE can store values like '2023-07-06'.
TIME: Used for time values (hour, minute, second).
DATETIME: Used for date and time values.
DATETIME can store values like '2023-07-06 13:45:30'.
TIMESTAMP: Used for date and time values, often with time zone information.
YEAR: Used for year values.
YEAR can store values like 2023.
BOOLEAN: Used for true/false values.
ENUM: Enumerated type, a string object with a value chosen from a list
SET: Similar to ENUM, but can store multiple values
SET('red', 'green', 'blue')
JSON types for storing structured data.
spatial data types for geographic information
